onboarding_tooltips_2022q4_2023q1.text: Every megawatt you own can be converted into a project: pick a use, then fill its three slots -- Power, Tenant, Capital. Nothing builds until all three are filled.
A megawatt is always doing exactly one thing: mining, hosting someone else's machines, leased to an AI tenant (shell), running your own GPUs (full stack), or sitting idle and costing you money.
Your credit rating (CCC to BBB) is new: Act I had no such meter. It's set by your leverage and the quality of your signed contracts, and it decides what any new lender will charge you.

Signing a long contract is worth more than the cash it brings in this quarter -- it adds to your contracted backlog, which the market rewards even before the money arrives. A hyperscaler's signature counts for more than an AI lab's.
A signed tenant sets a ready-by date. Miss it by a quarter and you pay a penalty. Miss it by two, and they might just leave.
Every site now carries a region tag. It's not just flavor -- power price, grid queue time, and how fast the neighbors turn on you all depend on where you build.

Not ready for a big tenant? A pilot cluster is the smallest way into AI: half a megawatt to two megawatts of your own GPUs, rented out at the going cloud price, with no tenant to win first. Expect them to sit idle some of the time (about 30% at first); you get better at it as you learn.

glossary.definition: Delayed-draw term loan: debt secured on your GPUs and their revenue contract, drawn down in stages as you buy more chips.
A contract where the tenant pays whether or not they actually use the capacity -- your protection against them walking away early.
The yield a buyer expects when purchasing a stabilized, leased asset. A lower cap rate means a higher sale price for the same rental income.
A big-tech guarantee that covers a weaker tenant's lease payments, in exchange for equity (usually warrants).
A building with power, cooling, and electrical infrastructure ready for GPUs, but no compute installed yet.
A GPU-cloud company (like CoreWeave or Nebius) that rents compute by the hour instead of running its own applications.
One GPU running for one hour -- the basic unit AI compute is priced and sold in.
Power Usage Effectiveness: total facility power divided by the power actually reaching the computers. Lower is more efficient.
Service-Level Agreement: the uptime and performance a tenant is guaranteed, with financial penalties if you miss it.
A partner funds most of a project's equity in exchange for most of its profit -- faster capital, smaller share.
Debt Service Coverage Ratio: how many times over your cash flow covers your debt payments. Lenders set a minimum.
The total remaining value of signed, not-yet-delivered revenue across all your tenant contracts.
The waiting list for scarce new GPUs during a shortage -- pay a premium to jump it, or wait.
The price for uncontracted GPU capacity sold on the open market, hour by hour -- volatile, and it can be cut overnight.
Owning the GPUs yourself, not just the building -- higher revenue, higher risk, and you eat the depreciation.
Renting out a powered building to a tenant who brings and owns their own GPUs.
A company like Microsoft, Google, Amazon, or Meta -- the highest-credit tenant you can sign.
A frontier AI company like OpenAI, Anthropic, or xAI -- pays well, but its credit is unproven.
A contract clause a tenant can invoke to suspend payments during extraordinary circumstances, without formally defaulting.
How many years you spread a GPU's cost over on your books -- a longer schedule flatters your reported profit.
A regional meter that rises with every megawatt built nearby, feeding protests and moratorium risk.
